title: Repair Streaming Moving Averages
instructions:
Fix two arithmetic bugs in `moving_average.py`: averages during warm-up and the running
sum when a sample is evicted. Preserve the existing public API and all behavior below.

`MovingAverage(window: int)` accepts positive integers only (bool is rejected), otherwise
raises `ValueError`. It retains the most recent window samples in arrival order.
- `add(value: int | float) -> float` adds a sample, evicts the oldest if necessary, and
  returns the arithmetic mean of the samples actually retained. Negative and zero values
  are valid. Bool, other types, NaN and infinities raise `ValueError` without changing state.
  Test numeric inputs are small enough for float conversion and summation.
- Read-only property `average -> float | None` returns the current mean, or None if empty.
- Read-only property `count -> int` is the number of retained samples.
- `snapshot() -> tuple[float, ...]` returns retained samples, oldest first, independently
  of later updates.
- `extend(values) -> list[float]` consumes any iterable once by calling add for each item;
  returns the successive averages. If an item is invalid, raise `ValueError`; earlier
  valid items from that call stay committed and later items are not consumed.
- `reset() -> None` empties samples and running sum but keeps the same window.
The public `window` attribute contains the configured size; callers do not change it.

- `moving_average.py`
